newsitem.title: GERMANY: FOCUS-Kohl committed to timely euro launch - Bonn.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Kohl committed to timely euro launch - Bonn.

text.p: A German government spokesman said on Monday Chancellor Helmut Kohl remained unalterably committed to a timely launch of Europe's single currency even though Kohl was now stressing the euro's stability was his top priority.

Trying to stifle speculation that Kohl's enthusiasm for the proposed single currency was waning, government spokesman Herbert Schmuelling told journalists at a news conference that Kohl's view on the euro had not changed.

Schmuelling rejected the suggestion that Kohl's comments broadcast on Sunday that he was opposed to a weak euro did not mean the chancellor had changed his firm belief that the euro should be launched on time in 1999.
"The chancellor said quite clearly that there would be no weak euro," Schmuelling said. "The schedule and the criteria remain valid as they were in the past. There has been no change in the mood."

In an interview with ZDF television aired on Sunday from his holiday in the Austrian Alps, Kohl said that even though he was committed to European integration he would not sacrifice monetary stability. He said he would not accept a weak euro.
"Whoever believes that Helmut Kohl will give up the policy (of stability) out of enthusiasm for Europe and day-to-day factors... is wrong. That is a price I will not pay."

Bavarian state premier Edmund Stoiber has in several recent newspaper interviews said the euro launch should be put back if countries overshoot the Maastricht budget deficit goal of three percent of gross domestic product.

Kohl has bowed to pressure from Stoiber and pledged to meet the strict 3.0 deficit percent interpretation of the budget deficit criteria to allay fears of those who believe a fudged currency union would result in a soft euro. -- Erik Kirschbaum, Bonn newsroom +49 228 260 97160
